items.title: Pure projective modules and universally exact resolutions by direct sums
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a module is pure projective exactly when it is a direct summand of a direct sum of finitely presented modules, and that every module fits into a universally exact sequence 0 -> N -> P -> M -> 0 with P pure projective (statement lines 2682-2691). The proof first notes that finitely presented modules are pure projective by the universal-exactness criterion, so direct summands of direct sums of them are pure projective; for the second part it writes M as a filtered colimit of finitely presented modules, forms the sequence 0 -> N -> the direct sum of the P_i -> M -> 0, observes that every map from a finitely presented module to M factors through some P_i, applies the universal-exactness criterion to conclude the sequence is universally exact, and finally derives the first part in the pure projective case by splitting (proof lines 2693-2710). The level is H3: both assertions are argued from the same displayed sequence, with the filtered-colimit factoring step and the splitting written out.
